analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and a new startup shape-warmup section around head lines 956-986. The supplied units cover head lines 1-797 of the document, which is mostly unchanged Nemotron Super and GLM5Next text; the added warmup section lies outside the supplied text. I found no code, config, authorization, attestation, encryption or key-handling change in the visible material.

The changes visible in the patch excerpt describe an excluded warmup that runs a greedy 128-token probe and shape cells under a 20-second wall budget. It uses the artifact's default sampling, and it trains no rates or counters. The excerpt is truncated, so I could not see the doc text about preload ordering or about the local-endpoint preemption caveat.

Relevant threat IDs are T-041, T-028 and T-029 (prefix cache, residual GPU data, idle GPU), plus A-001 and TB-007. Questions for later passes, none of which is a finding on this evidence:
- Whether the warmup prompts are synthetic. If they are, they cannot leak consumer data.
- Whether the warmup uses cacheScope or touches the SSD prefix cache. If it donates blocks to SSD, that could widen the T-041 at-rest surface.
- Whether warmup can delay registration or availability beyond the 20 s budget.

The docs correctly state that the warmup trains no counters and runs before registration. No threat-model assumption looks invalidated, and no model update is needed from the visible text. Because the implementing code is not in this batch, I set needs_deeper_review=true only to flag the truncated warmup section and the unseen code. The doc-only portion I examined has no security regression.
